independent_focused_validation.decision: The reported Major invalid derivation is established and correctly bounded; no scientific change to the current English report is needed.

checks.derivation: Using n=2(p+1)/(p-1), its K=(pS-p)(p-1)(d-2)S^2/48 equals (n-d)S^2/[3(n-2)^2]. Printed t=n-2 and delta=(n-d)/4 give 2delta S^2/(3t^2)=K/2. Thus rho<=K cannot justify discarding c1=2(K/2-rho). At d=3,n=4,p=3,S=1,rho=1/16, K=1/12, c1=-1/24 and c2=1/8.
checks.assessment: This is an admissible scalar test of the coefficient implication, not a constructed manifold/PDE counterexample; the original report preserves that distinction.

checks.derivation: The original parameter gives c1>=0,c2>0 under rho<=K/2. Under rho<K, choose delta=(n-d)/4+3t^2rho/(4S^2); then epsilon=t-1/2-delta>0, c1=K-rho and c2=3t^2(K-rho)/(2nS^2) are positive. At rho=K, c1>=0 forces delta/t^2 at least (n-d)/[2(n-2)^2], while c2>0 forces strictly less; varying t does not remove that conflict.
checks.assessment: Both stated repairs are valid within the displayed estimate; the equality endpoint is unproved by it, rather than disproved.

checks.derivation: For A=P^(n-1)v^(1-n), q=(n-2)/(n-1), A^q=P^(n-2)v^(2-n). Theta>=2(n-1) makes the Holder cutoff exponent nonnegative. The global inequality and V(B2R)=O(R^(2(n-1))) first give A integrable. The annular form then tends to zero, contradicting A>0. Theorem 4.5 requires little-o R^(2p/(p-1)), so it is not supplied by the original, weaker big-O condition.
checks.assessment: The main absorption derivation is Major under the contract. Fundamental P-function identities and the separate nonnegative-curvature classifications are not refuted.
